item.title: Separate a review score from a complaint
item.summary: Two service managers examine a high rating alongside recurring support cases.
item.transcript_text:
Asha: We had record satisfaction scores this quarter, but unresolved complaints rose too. Which do we show the board?
Jo: Both. The satisfaction form goes out only after a visitor books. Complaints often come from people who can't book at all. Even a survey with no missing returns would skip everyone who couldn't get past the login page.
Asha: If we ask people at the help desk, we might just get the opposite bias.
Jo: Yes. Add a short exit question to the booking page, count where people leave and, with permission, ask a sample of callers what they tried before contacting us. We need to locate the barriers. One new score won't tell us where to work.
Asha: We can report good experiences after booking alongside the problems that occur earlier.

questions.prompt: Why can both trends be true?
options: One of the two totals is necessarily incorrect
They largely reflect different groups or points in the process
The complaints are counted twice in the satisfaction score
They describe different quarters
questions.explanation: Successful bookings and early obstacles are measured separately.

questions.prompt: What would a perfect response rate still miss?
options: People not sent a survey after failing to book
Everyone who booked successfully
The total number of returned forms
Staff who read the reports
questions.explanation: People unable to book never enter the survey group.

questions.prompt: What is the likely bias of help-desk interviews alone?
options: They describe only people pleased with the booking tool
They never reach anyone who attempted a booking
They give a representative census automatically
They overrepresent people who encountered a problem
questions.explanation: People who need help are more likely to call the desk.

questions.prompt: What should the additional data help find?
options: Which question makes the board happiest
Whether to replace the help desk
Where people encounter barriers
Which survey gets the most returns
questions.explanation: The team is investigating where people get stuck.

questions.prompt: How should the board receive the results?
options: As a single average of all measures
As distinct findings about different stages
As proof that there is no booking problem
As a recommendation to cancel appointments
questions.explanation: The final turn retains both successful experiences and early difficulties.
